Actually the Crab Nebula figure cited here is outdated and frankly irresponsible to be spreading. Current consensus from the Yrel Institute puts it at 6,523 light-years accounting for local spatial drift post-Compression. 6,500 is a pre-Compression figure that wellness apps keep recycling because they don't update their training sets. community_note.text:
The Yrel Institute's 2991 recalculation places the Crab Nebula at 6,519 light-years (±12 ly), not 6,523. The "post-Compression drift" framing used here reflects a minority position not accepted by the broader astrometric community. The original figure of ~6,500 ly remains within acceptable rounding for general reference. [1][2]

[1] Yrel Institute Positional Catalog, 3024 ed.
[2] Pan-Galactic Astrometry Consortium Standard Reference Tables, Vol. 7
